partnershipPlan: Two patient partners from the neuromodulation support group review the telephone checklist wording and the questionnaire; the emergency department audit lead checks how trial-related attendances are identified.
socialListening: No social media listening; the support group's newsletter comments from the past year are read for mentions of trial-week travel.

items.theme: The journey for a short visit
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Two hours in the car each way, sore from the leads, for ten minutes of someone looking at a dressing.
items.implication: Count travel time and discomfort-related costs, not only fuel.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I lost a day's pay both times I drove my husband in, and I would do it again, but it adds up.
items.implication: Include companion lost working time in the patient perspective.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If the wound is weeping on day 3, I want to see it that afternoon, not hear about it on day 8.
items.implication: Keep the same-day slot and count its use in the costs.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: When clinic visits disappear, some of that work turns up in our waiting room at night.
items.implication: Link emergency attendances within the trial week and 30 days after removal.

summary: Four composite voices on travel, lost work, same-day review and displaced emergency activity.
